reason: H0 exercises only the contiguous-buffer API through spng_set_png_buffer. It never invokes the distinct streaming callback protocol exposed by spng_set_png_stream, including callback errors and fragmented or truncated reads. In S1, streaming changes allocation and read behavior: read_data may reallocate ctx->data, discard_chunk_bytes performs repeated SPNG_READ_SIZE reads, and get_idat_bytes selects streaming-specific input lengths. These paths are attacker-controlled through the read callback and are materially fuzz-worthy but unreachable from H0.
evidence: H0 calls spng_set_png_buffer(ctx, (void*)data, size) and never calls spng_set_png_stream.
spng_set_png_stream installs a user-supplied spng_read_fn, stores read_user_ptr, allocates an 8192-byte buffer, and sets ctx->streaming = 1.
read_data calls ctx->read_fn and conditionally reallocates ctx->data only when ctx->streaming is set.
discard_chunk_bytes uses repeated SPNG_READ_SIZE reads only for streaming contexts; buffer-backed contexts use one read_chunk_bytes call.
get_idat_bytes has a ctx->streaming branch that limits reads to SPNG_READ_SIZE.
recommended_action: Add a streaming-input fuzz harness using spng_set_png_stream with fuzz-controlled fragmentation, EOF/error returns, and chunk-boundary splits, while retaining the existing image and chunk limits.
